intro.title: For Roma in Moldova, building a future means navigating compounding disadvantages in an uncertain present
intro.content:
Roma face disadvantages across education, work, housing, health and public services — with discrimination cutting through all of them. These pressures compound: exclusion in one area narrows what is possible in the next, so barriers accumulate within households and shape opportunities for the next generation.

Shared barriers affect people differently depending on the circumstance. Gender, age or place pull households onto different paths. Women are less likely to enter paid work, while men’s greater access often leads to informal jobs with little protection. For children, frequent moves can interrupt schooling; for older people, securing treatment and care becomes a greater concern. Where families live shapes these paths too: home ownership can offer little security amid worn-out infrastructure and arrears, and nearby services can remain out of reach because of discrimination.

Despite this, Roma families continue to pursue better lives. They assemble strategies from seasonal, informal or entrepreneurial work, undertake care and housing labour for each other, and strive for their children to stay at school. They are resilient, managing what the day demands while aspiring for better and secure lives.
